description: Hybrid profile: the HEAVY tiers (code.generate, chat.deep) run on a remote OpenAI-compatible LiteLLM proxy; everything latency-sensitive or high-volume stays on local Ollama. The remote key is NOT here - api_key_env names the environment variable, and HostProfile.Validate() refuses to start if it is unset (doc 6.2 fail-fast). To run with no remote at all, copy host-profile.local-only.example.json over this file.

litellm.note: LiteLLM proxy, OpenAI-compatible. The base URL INCLUDES /v1: the proxy answers on both / and /v1, but /v1 is the canonical OpenAI root and is what /chat/completions is appended to.

chat.fast.note: ASPIRATIONAL: no genuinely small model is installed, so this is the same 9B as chat.balanced. Pull llama3.2:3b (~2GB) to make this tier real.

chat.deep.note: REMOTE. This tier was aspirational while it pointed at the same 9B as chat.balanced; it is now a genuinely deeper model. coder-120b is a REASONING model - it spends completion tokens thinking before emitting an answer, so callers on this tier need a generous max_tokens or they get an empty completion (the provider reports that as a named error rather than a silent empty success).

classify.intent.note: Stays local on purpose: classification is high-volume and latency-sensitive, and a remote round trip per classification would dominate the loop.

embed.text.note: Stays local. The proxy also fronts nomic-embed-text, but embeddings are called constantly (KG enrichment, semantic grounding) and the stored vectors must stay comparable - switching the embedding model would invalidate every embedding already in the graph.

code.generate.note: REMOTE. The 120B coder, in place of the local 7B. This is the tier the synthesis comparison is about.

code.fast.note: Stays local on purpose - this is the fast/cheap path, and keeping it local preserves a working local coder when the remote is unavailable.
